title: Checking Walter Allen's King Oliver personnel for February 1934
summary: Dupre reads personnel from Allen's book and Phillips confirms it, including Red Elkins, Selmer Payne, Dan Andrews and Billy Coleman; the band was based in Hopkinsville, Kentucky.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: I looked at this book called King Joe Oliver, a little
Phillips - 159
book written by a guy named Walter C. Allen. I read the personnel that was listed in there.
King Joe Oliver?
Yeah, that's the name of the book.
Did it give the list of the guys in the band?

Yeah. I already read this to you, so I'm going to read it to you again. They had some notes written by Paul barnes. He's the guy who wrote out this itinerary I showed you. So maybe we can talk to that a little bit; that would be good. But let me talk about the personnel first. In the book this was listed as the February 24, 1934 personnel. The personnel listed then was Herman "Red" Elkins, you and King Oliver on trumpets; Pete Jones on trombone; Buddy Harold and Paul Barnes on altos.
Yeah.
Selmer Payne on tenor.
That's right.
Charles Toran on piano. Bernie Cobb on guitar. Dan Andrews on string bass.
Yeah.
Dewitt Debo Mill on drums. Billy Coleman...
Was in front.
Director. And Dorris Duff...
Singing.
Phillips - 160
Male vocalist. And Ross McConnell was the booking agent.
Yeah.
It says here that at that time they were based in Hopkinsville, Kentucky.
Yeah.
And the landlady they stayed with was Mrs. Mildred Clark.
I don't know. I probably was gone then.
Well, this is February of '34.
Yeah, but see, when they left Hopkinsville, I didn't go back no more.
But you were up in the band until July 5, 1934, right?
Yeah.
So you would have been in there for a few months after this time. Was that personnel right?
Yeah, that's right. But see, we stayed there when we first went to Hopkinsville.
At Mrs. Mildred Clark's place?
Yeah.
Do you remember her?
See, after we left there and went back on the road, I didn't go back no more. Because the bus got burned up and everything after we left there.
I read in the book that she gave some parties for the musicians while you guys were staying there.
